paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The plot compares the training loss over time for two models: Vanilla Transformer and SepLLM. The x-axis represents training time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds, with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 50,000 seconds. The y-axis represents the loss, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. The Vanilla Transformer is depicted by a purple dashed line with triangle markers, starting at a loss of approximately 2.75 at 0 seconds and decreasing to around 2.52 at 250,000 seconds. The SepLLM is shown by a red dashed line with circular markers, starting at approximately 2.72 at 0 seconds and decreasing to about 2.48 at 250,000 seconds. Throughout the training period, SepLLM consistently maintains a lower loss than the Vanilla Transformer. A green dashed rectangle highlights the region from 200,000 to 250,000 seconds, with an annotation indicating a 1.26× improvement, suggesting a relative performance gain in this phase. A horizontal green dashed line at loss = 2.50 serves as a reference threshold.
